moved.sentence: **High-complexity algorithms warrant their own scope group.** Code implementing O(n log n) or worse algorithms on large datasets is a distinct engineering concern — performance optimization, testing with large inputs, and benchmarking apply specifically to it.

judged.note: should-give-high-complexity-algorithms-own-scope-group keeps the own-scope-group call at SHOULD for O(n log n)-or-worse code on large datasets; the rationale keeps the distinct-concern reason (optimization, large-input testing, benchmarking).

moved.sentence: **Caching layers are scope group candidates.** A caching subsystem with its own eviction policy, invalidation logic, and hit/miss tracking is a meaningful independent component.

judged.note: should-treat-caching-layers-as-candidates keeps caching subsystems with eviction, invalidation and hit/miss tracking as candidates; the rationale keeps the meaningful-independent-component reason.

moved.sentence: **Computational code should not be mixed with I/O.** Files that mix algorithm implementation with network calls or file system access conflate two different concerns — note this as a design smell.

judged.note: The two rules keep not mixing computation with I/O and noting such files as a design smell; the rationale keeps the conflated-concerns reason and the network/file-system scope.

moved.sentence: **Simple CRUD code is not a boundary signal.** Code that maps data structures to/from persistence formats and performs no interesting computation is not algorithmically significant — its boundaries come from `module-boundaries` or `purpose-classification`.

judged.note: should-not-treat-crud-as-boundary-signal keeps the claim and the module-boundaries / purpose-classification redirect; the rationale keeps the no-interesting-computation definition.

moved.sentence: **Parallel computation implies a concurrency concern.** Code using parallel execution primitives has distinct testing requirements (race conditions, thread safety) and likely belongs in its own scope group or must be flagged as a concurrency concern.

judged.note: must-scope-or-flag-parallel-computation keeps own-scope-group-or-MUST-flag; the rationale keeps the race-condition and thread-safety testing reason.
